headline: Broad-based sales growth lifts margins and earnings
summary_short: Henry Schein's Q2 FY2026 net sales rose 6.7% y/y to $3.458 billion across all three segments, with gross margin expanding to 31.8% from 31.4% and diluted EPS of $0.82, up from $0.70 a year ago.
summary_long: Net sales rose 6.7% y/y to $3.458 billion, led by all three segments: Distribution & Value-Added Services (+6.6%), Specialty Products (+8.7%), and Technology (+8.2%). Gross margin expanded to 31.8% from 31.4% on favorable mix and early value-creation-initiative benefits. Operating income rose 13.2% y/y to $171 million despite $29 million of restructuring costs under the ongoing 2024 Plan. Diluted EPS was $0.82, up from $0.70, aided by a lower diluted share count following continued buybacks ($6.3 billion repurchased to date, $455 million remaining authorization). Shareholders' equity fell to $3.157 billion from $3.445 billion on buyback-driven reductions; cash rose to $157 million from $145 million. No forward guidance was disclosed in the filing.

drivers.explanation: All three segments grew: distribution on dental/medical merchandise and equipment demand, Specialty Products on implant/biomaterial growth plus acquisitions, Technology on rising cloud practice-management adoption.
Margin expansion was attributed to favorable business/customer mix and early benefits from value-creation initiatives, plus product-mix gains in Specialty Products and Technology.
Higher gross profit drove the increase, partly offset by $29 million of restructuring and related costs under the ongoing 2024 Plan.
EPS growth outpaced net income growth because weighted diluted shares fell to 114.4 million from 122.6 million a year ago, consistent with continued buybacks.
The year-over-year decline is consistent with continued share repurchases ($6.3 billion cumulative, $455 million remaining authorization) outpacing retained earnings growth.
